**Yes — the documents contradict each other on remote work, in several distinct ways.** The contradiction scanner has three verified flags in total, and two of them concern remote work (one of those is marked resolved, one open). Beyond the flagged pairs, the remote-work passages also disagree on core hours, eligibility and stipend mechanics.

## 1. How many days may an employee work remotely? (direct conflict)
- **v1:** "Employees may work remotely for up to **3 days** per calendar week. The remaining working days must be spent at the assigned office location." [remote_work_policy_v1 § 2. Remote Work Allowance]
- **v2:** "Employees must work from their assigned office at least **4 days** per calendar week. Remote work is limited to a maximum of **1 day** per week and requires written approval from the direct manager for each remote day." [remote_work_policy_v2 § 2. Office Attendance]

These are incompatible weekly limits (3 remote days vs. 1 remote day). Note that v2 is dated later (effective 2025-06-01) than v1 (effective 2024-01-01) [remote_work_policy_v2 § ACME Hybrid Work Policy (v2.0)] [remote_work_policy_v1 § Acme Corporation], but **neither document states that it supersedes or repeals the other** — so the documents themselves do not resolve which limit applies.

## 2. Who is covered (flagged by the scanner as an open contradiction)
- **v1:** applies to "all full-time employees in **engineering, design, and support** functions. Contractors and interns are covered by separate agreements." [remote_work_policy_v1 § 1. Purpose]
- **v2:** applies to "all full-time employees in **every function**." [remote_work_policy_v2 § 1. Purpose]

## 3. Eligibility thresholds (also inconsistent)
- **v1:** eligible after "**6 months** of continuous employment"; employees on a performance improvement plan are not eligible. [remote_work_policy_v1 § 4. Eligibility]
- **v2:** "only to employees who have completed **12 months** of continuous employment and who hold a performance rating of 'meets expectations' or higher." [remote_work_policy_v2 § 4. Eligibility]

## 4. Core hours (inconsistent)
- **v1:** reachable "between **10:00 and 16:00** local time." [remote_work_policy_v1 § 6. Core Hours]
- **v2:** reachable "between **09:00 and 17:00** local time." [remote_work_policy_v2 § 6. Core Hours]

## 5. Remote-work pay/equipment (flagged by the scanner; marked resolved)
- **sample_policy (RW-2025-014, eff. 2025-03-01):** a **$50/month** internet stipend for employees remote at least three days per week, "requires **no receipts**", plus a one-time **$600** equipment budget; its tier table lists Bronze 3 days/$50/$400, Silver 4 days/$60/$600, Gold 5 days/$75/$800. [sample_policy § Policy Number: RW-2025-014. Effective Date: March 1, 2025.]
- **expense_policy:** home internet reimbursed up to **$60/month**, and "Each category requires an **itemized receipt**"; unclaimed amounts are forfeited. [expense_policy § 2. Reimbursable Categories]

So the same home-internet benefit is described as a no-receipt $50 stipend in one document and a receipt-based $60 cap in another, and the Gold tier's $75/month exceeds the $60 cap. The scanner records this pair as a verified contradiction that has since been marked resolved — the documents as ingested do not themselves show an amendment reconciling the two figures.

## 6. Equipment provisioning (minor inconsistency)
- **v1:** "a laptop and a security token." [remote_work_policy_v1 § 5. Equipment and Security]
- **v2:** "a laptop, a security token, and a **monitor**," with VPN plus multi-factor authentication. [remote_work_policy_v2 § 5. Equipment]

## Bottom line
The corpus does not present a single consistent remote-work rule. The sharpest conflict is the weekly remote-day allowance (3 days vs. 1 day), followed by scope, eligibility, core hours and the internet-stipend terms. The documents contain no statement of precedence between v1 and v2, so **the ingested documents do not say which version governs** — that is a gap, not something I can infer.
